who: the holder of a Binance USD-M position whose margin ratio crossed maintenance, closed by the venue's own risk engine — paying an explicit Liquidation Clearance Fee to Binance/the Insurance Fund and market impact to whoever is resting on the book when the IOC sweeps it (in the extreme, to opposing profitable traders via ADL)
why_they_keep_paying: The payment is not a decision: Binance's own protocol states that at maintenance breach the system issues an Immediate-or-Cancel order, fills it as far as the book allows, cancels the remainder, and deducts a Liquidation Clearance Fee of notional × rate (BTCUSDT's insurance clearance rate was raised from 0.30 % to 0.60 % on 2021-06-08), with any bankrupt remainder absorbed by the Insurance Fund and then by ADL. They keep doing it because leverage is the product — the venue sells it, the Insurance Fund is capitalised out of these very fees, and the same design (risk-engine close, liquidation fee funding an insurance fund, ADL as last resort) exists on Bybit, OKX, Deribit and on-chain on Hyperliquid, so it is structural to the instrument and not an artefact of one exchange.
what_would_end_it: Replacing forced market closure with a mechanism that does not execute against the public book — a timed margin call, an auction, or socialised/portfolio-level netting — or removing leverage from the product. Short of that, only the intensity moves: leverage caps (125x → 20x for new accounts, 2021-07-19, extended 2021-07-27) and per-symbol margin-tier tightening shrink the leveraged base without ending the payment.
notes: The payer is real and documented; four things in the evidence cut against this hypothesis' route to it. (1) TRIGGER IS NOT IN THE PANEL. Binance states liquidation 'always occurs at Mark Price', which is index-anchored precisely so that local perp wicks do not liquidate anyone. So a displaced 4-hour perp candle is neither necessary nor sufficient for a maintenance breach — the proposal's caveat that price is 'evidence not measurement' understates it: the trigger variable is a different series than the one CCI reads. (2) THE FOOTPRINT IS ENGINEERED SMALL. 'Smart Liquidation' issues one large IOC intended to reduce the margin deficit *without* fully closing the position, filling as much as the book allows and cancelling the rest — partial and capped by design, which is the opposite of the sustained one-directional flow a 'cascade then relaxation' reading needs. (3) THE ASYMMETRY RUNS AGAINST THE RELAXATION HALF. The forced BUY (liquidated short) is the minority leg: GEV work on BitMEX perp data puts 3.51 % of longs vs 1.89 % of shorts liquidated daily, average leverage ~60x among liquidated accounts. The buy-side flow the reversion reading is built on is the smaller, rarer half of the payer — consistent with cci_reversion having scored 0 of 9 unconditionally in H0017. (4) NOT STATIONARY ACROSS 2019–2024. Inside the development window the fee doubled (0.30 %→0.60 %, 2021-06-08), the leverage cap fell (125x→20x for new accounts, 2021-07-19, widened 2021-07-27), and margin tiers were retuned per symbol (FTT 2022-11-08, BLZ 2023-08-14, TRB). The payer's existence is durable; its size and threshold location are not, so any single pooled estimate mixes regimes. Also: even possessing the feed would not fix the measurement gap — since 2021-04-27 the public !forceOrder stream pushes only the single largest liquidation per symbol per 1000 ms, and Coinglass-style totals are modelled from open interest and assumed leverage rather than engine records. Published cascade research (arXiv 2607.27070) finds forced flow is not reliably identifiable from price alone: the critical-slowing-down signature appears in 5 of 7 BTC cascades and is absent exactly in the news-shock ones. Finally, on who can collect: the explicit Clearance Fee goes to Binance and the Insurance Fund and is capturable by no trader; only the market-impact component is contestable, and liquidation levels are sold as a public heatmap product, so that component is the most crowded part of the payment.
